text:
incident_bot: Pager: p99 latency spike on cont-batching path in prod-usw2 · 12:03 UTC · auto-escalate to #eng-oncall :rotating_light:
incident_bot: Alerts: p95=420ms -> 1.1s, p99=1.2s -> 3.2s; streaming stalls reported, error rate unchanged (0.02%) · traces show long wait in batch-queue for mixed-seqlen customers
maria_oncall: saw the alert, looking now. Any customer-visible 5xxs?
cassie_support: Support: a handful of customers reported slow streaming responses, no 5xxs. Ticket count up 8 in last 10m. Customers mention intermittent long stalls during streaming chunks.
liam_sre: I'm pulling scheduler metrics. Uploading quick snapshot in thread. Preliminary: contbatch queue depth spiked, avg batch size jumped to 58, variance high due to many short+long seq mixing.
zahra_infra: repro trace: request waited ~850ms in queue, then downstream run was fine. Likely scheduling fairness + pack amplification.
maria_oncall: ok, summarize impact: p99 SLO (2s) breached for 30m window in prod-usw2, ~12% of requests above threshold, high for streaming customers.
kevin_prod: flagged to product: some PLG customers on streaming pipelines may notice lag. Notifying account leads for top 5.
liam_sre: quick mitigation options: 1) reduce max_batch_size on contbatch to 32 for prod-usw2; 2) enable preemptive hedging for streaming (drop into stream path after X ms); 3) increase fairness weight for short requests to avoid tail amplification. Prefer 1+2 to push latency back under SLO fast.
maria_oncall: do we have a safe flag flip path?
zahra_infra: yes, feature flags via /ops/flags service. I'll run a canary on 2 nodes first. Command:```bash
/ops/flags set contbatch.max_batch=32 --env=prod-usw2 --scope=nodes:2
```
liam_sre: also running a temporary KV-cache conservative eviction to reduce cache churn:```json
{"kv_evict_mode":"aggressive","kv_ttl_ms":120000}
```
cassie_support: post a short customer update: "We're investigating increased streaming latency in US-WEST2. No errors, working on mitigation."
kevin_prod: thanks — please cc the top accounts.
zahra_infra: canary started on 2 nodes. Observing batch size median drop to 34 on those nodes, p99 on those nodes down to ~1.4s.
maria_oncall: good. Roll to rest of prod-usw2? Risk?
liam_sre: low risk but monitor KV eviction side-effects (cold cache misses). We'll roll gradually and watch CPU. I'll add a clamped rollout: 30% -> 60% -> 100% with 2m between steps. Command:```bash
/ops/flags rollout contbatch.max_batch=32 --env=prod-usw2 --steps=30,60,100 --pause=120s
```
zahra_infra: starting rollout.
(2m later)
zahra_infra: rollout at 30% complete. p99 aggregated down to 2.1s, p95 back to ~520ms. Queue depths dropping.
liam_sre: enabling stream hedging for all streaming routes as secondary measure:```bash
/ops/flags set streaming.hedge_delay_ms=250 --env=prod-usw2
```
maria_oncall: enabling now.
(30s later)
liam_sre: hedging engaged, streaming tail spikes reduced on canary nodes. End-to-end p99 now ~1.8s region-wide. Looks promising.
cassie_support: customers getting updates, some report improvement.
kevin_prod: recommend we keep reduced batch size until end of day and follow-up with scheduling fairness tuning in next maintenance window.
maria_oncall: agreed. Create follow-up ticket for fairness weight tuning + analysis of mixed-seqlen patterns.
liam_sre: created ticket INF-2042: "contbatch fairness tuning & mixed-seqlen mitigation" — includes graphs and suggested changes (per-class weights, dynamic batching thresholds).
zahra_infra: rolling to 60% -> now at 60%. No CPU spike so far.
maria_oncall: any customer impact from KV eviction?
liam_sre: we saw a small uptick in tail RPS on first requests (cold hits) but within tolerance. Will monitor.
cassie_support: updating customer comms: "We've rolled mitigations and will monitor — follow-up with root cause and timeline tomorrow."
kevin_prod: good. Who is taking next 2-hour handoff?
maria_oncall: alex_oncall taking next handoff window. I'm handing over current state: mitigations deployed (max_batch=32, stream hedging 250ms, kv-evict conservative), p99 at ~1.7-1.9s, monitoring dashboards linked.
alex_oncall: on it. I'll keep watch and escalate if p99 goes above 2.2s or error rate increases.
maria_oncall: logging final notes for handoff: steps ran, commands used, ticket INF-2042 created, customer comms sent. Marking incident as under mitigation. :white_check_mark:
